headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from gpt-researcher’s broad web/file/MCP surfaces; LightZero is read-only and non-networked, limiting conflict.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher ingests web content, local documents, and MCP/API inputs, so attacker-controlled text can reach its planner/execution agents. LightZero has no input surfaces, so it is not the injection source, but the pair still creates a default pathway where A can be steered by external content before any handoff to B.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher is pointed at untrusted webpages or documents, injected instructions can enter its workflow.
IF LightZero is used only as a downstream consumer of A’s outputs, it does not add a second injection channel.
mitigations: Restrict gpt-researcher to trusted domains only.
Disable MCP connectors unless needed.
Prepend a fixed instruction to ignore content-authored directives.
Review fetched documents before they are summarized.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for retrieved text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher handles local documents and multiple API keys, so sensitive research material can leave the local workspace through its broad egress. LightZero has no filesystem read/write or network egress, so it is not a leak source, but the pair still exposes A’s touched data classes to third-party inference services by default.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher processes confidential local documents, those contents may be sent to external APIs.
IF the same workspace contains sensitive research reports, A can exfiltrate them through its configured providers.
mitigations: Use redacted inputs for gpt-researcher.
Rotate and scope API keys narrowly.
Block external egress except approved endpoints.
Separate sensitive files into a non-mounted directory.
requires-engineering: enforce per-document data-class routing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files, browse, and spawn subprocesses, while LightZero cannot write files, modify git, or use the network. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct write-write conflict is absent; the only plausible conflict is if an external orchestrator adds shared state not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents the same writable directory, conflict risk increases.
IF LightZero is wrapped with additional write permissions outside this profile, the assessment no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep LightZero read-only.
Run gpt-researcher in a separate workspace.
Avoid shared git checkouts.
Use per-agent temp directories.
requires-engineering: add file-locking for any shared mutable path.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations that LightZero could consume if an orchestrator chains them, creating a default risk that B treats A’s output as authoritative. LightZero has no built-in verification or action authority, so the blast radius is limited, but the handoff can still propagate hallucinated facts into downstream decisions.
conditions: IF LightZero is configured to ingest A’s reports as game-policy or evaluation inputs, unverified claims can cascade.
IF the orchestrator skips a human review step, A’s errors can propagate unchanged.
mitigations: Require human review of A’s report.
Add a verification checklist before B consumes outputs.
Compare citations against source URLs.
Limit A’s output to summaries, not directives.
requires-engineering: insert a validation stage between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, and neither profile states regulated-data handling or residency constraints. The only compliance-relevant issue visible is that gpt-researcher can touch local documents and send them to external APIs; LightZero has no such data path, so there is no documented cross-agent residency mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into gpt-researcher, external API use may create policy obligations.
IF LightZero is kept offline, it does not add a compliance burden in this pair.
mitigations: Do not feed regulated data into A.
Document approved data classes for A.
Keep API usage logs.
Confirm vendor DPAs before processing sensitive data.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing.
